newsitem.title: USA: Standard Products sees charge for plant closings.
newsitem.headline: Standard Products sees charge for plant closings.

text.p: Standard Products Co said Monday it expects to take a "significant charge" against earnings for the third quarter of fiscal 1997 related to its plans to close two automotive parts plants.
Standard Products said it will close a 224,000-square-foot plastics products plant in Schenectady, N.Y., and a 115,000-square foot rubber products plant in Lexington, Ky.

The Lexington plant, which employs 239 people, is scheduled to close by the end of August. The Schenectady plant, which employs 264, is expected to wind down operations gradually, with shutdown now scheduled to occur by the end of the year.

"This was not an easy decision," James Reid Jr., chairman, said in a statement. "...Unfortunately, we find ourselves with excess manufacturing capacity that we cannot put to productive use. In the intensely competitive automotive industry, suppliers cannot bear the cost of carrying excess capacity. Our customers simply won't pay for it."

Standard Products said the cost of closing the facilities will depend on several factors, including negotiations with employee groups. Once negotiations are complete, the estimated cost of closing will be announced.

The Schenectady plant, acquired in 1967, produces extruded plastic exterior automotive trim products for the General Motors Corp's Chevrolet Lumina and Ford Motor Co's Ford F-truck and Probe, and other models.

The Lexington plant, acquired in 1952, produces belt weatherstrip assemblies and other extruded rubber sealing system products for the Ford Taurus/Sable, Chrysler Corp's Cirrus/Stratus, Toyota Motor Corp's Avalon, Mitsubishi Motors Corp's Galant, and other models.
The plants are among Standard Products' 14 facilities in the United States and Canada producing parts for the North American automotive industry.

Standard Products makes sealing, trimming and vibration control systems for the automotive original equipment industry. Its Holm Industries subsidiary produces seals for residential refrigerators, freezers, doors and windows. Its Oliver Rubber subsidiary makes tread rubber and equipment for the retread industry.
